Subject: Post-call: Pricing & regional cost implications (US vs EU) for FintechCo

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the demo time. Quick recap from our discovery + a few clarifying questions so we can put together a tight cost estimate and recommended configuration:

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary workload: user-facing conversational flow + 1:1 summarization for compliance (short to medium prompts)
- Expected monthly tokens (combined inference + context): 50M-200M tokens/month initially, with spikes up to ~6M tokens/day during peak marketing events
- Preferred models: evaluating both open quantized variants (redwood-verified) for cost, and a higher-quality Llama 2-type variant for key flows
- Data residency: EU residency is a requirement for production (GDPR/compliance); sandbox/proof-of-concept can run in US region
- Budget signal: rough committed budget range of $8k- $25k/mo depending on model choice and SLA

Questions for you (quick replies appreciated so we can model unit economics):
1) Can you confirm the 50M-200M/month range (or give a tighter expected number)? Is that active tokens (responses) or total tokens including prompts/context?
2) Do you need all traffic served from EU by day 1, or is a staged approach (EU for production, US for experimentation) acceptable?
3) SLA/latency targets - are 200-400ms p50 acceptable for production, or do you need sub-100ms targets for certain flows?
4) Any preference on caching/response staleness for the summarization flow (that affects cost a lot)?

What we’ll provide next: a short unit-economics sheet showing: (a) baseline hosted US pricing per 1M tokens, (b) estimated EU region delta (infrastructure + data residency overhead), and (c) committed/reserved pricing options (3/6/12 month) with examples for 50M and 200M tokens/mo. I’ll include an attachment stub with the initial rollup.

Next steps: if that works, I’ll run the model and we can sync for 30 minutes Thurs/Fri to review.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_rollup.xlsx (spreadsheet - pricing scenarios)

Thanks,
Sean

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the recap — very helpful. Quick answers inline:
1) Token volumes: the 50M-200M is our best estimate for months 1-6. That’s total tokens (prompt + response). Realistically we expect closer to 80M/mo after month 2 if opt for the higher-quality model; the 200M is more of a long tail/peak during product campaigns.
2) EU residency: production must be EU-resident (data + model inference in EU) - sandbox can run in US. So yes, we need EU serving for go-live.
3) Latency: p50 ~200-300ms is fine for most user flows; backend summarization can be looser (p50 < 1s).
4) Caching: we’d like prefix caching for repeated prompts (customer profile lookups) but not for summaries - freshness is required there.

Budget: for RFP purposes the leadership has indicated an upper bound near $25k/mo for the first year (they prefer to buy committed capacity if the unit economics look good). As a benchmarking target, they’re hoping for ~$40-$70 per 1M tokens for the higher-quality model and ideally <$40 for heavily quantized variants.

Would appreciate your EU vs US delta and also an example SLA + committed discount path. Can do Thu 10:00 CET to review - works for Tom and me.

Best,
Sarah

Thanks Sarah - super helpful. Attached is a short PDF that walks through the EU vs US delta and two committed scenarios for the volumes you called out (attached: eu-region-cost-breakdown.pdf). High-level summary below so you can share with leadership quickly:

High-level unit economics (examples):
- Hosted (US region) - higher-quality model: $45 per 1M tokens
- Hosted (US region) - quantized variant: $28 per 1M tokens
- Hosted (EU region conservative delta +25%) - higher-quality model: $56.25 per 1M tokens
- Hosted (EU region conservative delta +25%) - quantized variant: $35 per 1M tokens

Committed pricing (illustrative):
- 3mo commit: ~10% off hosted list
- 6mo commit: ~20% off hosted list (we can get to ~ $45 * 0.8 = $36 per 1M for higher-quality in EU in some cases with committed capacity and configuration tuning)
- 12mo commit: ~30% off hosted list (best unit economics for heavy volume)

Notes and caveats:
- The EU delta captures higher infra costs, in-region KMS and additional networking/VPC overhead. If they are open to a hybrid approach (EU for production, US for non-customer-data experimental traffic) we can optimize cost further.
- If FintechCo wants guaranteed sub-100ms p50 for certain flows we’ll need a dedicated pool (Reserved/Dedicated) which changes the cost model - but it’s predictable and often better at scale.
- We intentionally left out log egress charges in the quick table - if they need long-term retention and export outside EU that will add additional costs.
